study type: Prospective observational cohort study with comparative groups
outcome: Diagnosis of early postpartum pelvic organ prolapse (POP)
cohort: The study included 150 pregnant patients at various gestational ages, 110 primiparas at 42-45 days post-delivery, and 55 healthy non-childbearing women.
finding: As gestational weeks progressed, PRM elasticity increased while LAM thickness decreased, and PRM elasticity and LAM thickness progressively decreased, and LH dimensions increased sequentially across control, cesarean section, and vaginal delivery groups, with a combination of LHA, PRM elasticity, and LAM thickness showing the highest diagnostic efficiency for early postpartum POP.
mod_finding: In both vaginal delivery and cesarean section groups, the elasticity of the PRM and the thickness of the LAM progressively decreased, while the LH area, perimeter, LHAP diameter, and LHLD increased sequentially, with their combination demonstrating the highest diagnostic efficiency for POP.
